boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:20 opens the outer court's gate circuit on a measure notice rather than a vayiqtol verb, מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ (oshb:Ezek.40.20) 'he measured its length and its width', immediately after the outer court's whole-court span closes at 40:19. The row measures the outer north gate (40:20-23), keyed to the first gate's own dimensions, הָיָ֔ה כְּמִדַּ֖ת הַשַּׁ֣עַר הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן (oshb:Ezek.40.21) 'was like the measure of the first gate', a phrase standing only at 40:21 in the chapter (sweep: 1 verse), and the outer south gate (40:24-27), keyed instead by כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.40.24) 'according to these measurements', a refrain recurring at 40:24, 40:28, 40:29, 40:32, 40:33 and 40:35 (sweep: 6 verses across chapter 40); the row carries four of the ch-40 doubled K/Q verses (40:21, 40:22, 40:24, 40:26) plus a single note at 40:25, every one the recurring ketiv-defective/qere-plene 3ms possessive-suffix pattern on chambers, posts, porches, windows and palm trees, never on the cubit figures themselves. A transport verb sits inside this row at 40:24, וַיּוֹלִכֵ֨נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם (oshb:Ezek.40.24) 'he led me toward the south', moving from the north gate to the south gate within the same outer court; it is disclosed as intra-row sub-onset texture, not the row seam, because it changes compass direction but not court. Close side: 40:27 ends the south outer gate on its hundred-cubit span to the inner court's south gate, וַיָּ֨מָד מִשַּׁ֧עַר אֶל הַשַּׁ֛עַר דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַדָּר֖וֹם מֵאָ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת (oshb:Ezek.40.27), immediately before 40:28's court-change transport verb. The seam at 40:27/40:28 turns on a location change -- the next verse's transport verb crosses from the outer court into the inner court -- unlike the compass-direction transport at 40:24 inside this row.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) 'he brought me out into the outer court ... then he brought me into the room' -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function, delivered as a genuine speak-formula, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) 'he said to me': these are the holy chambers where the priests eat the most holy things and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. Both the double transport at onset and the speak-formula at close are tier-1 devices, a stronger onset-and-close pairing than a bare content shift would give, despite the total absence of parashah corroboration in these chapters.
